injections.original_text: In all simulations, the electron injection index is fixed at $p=2.8$ to reproduce the commonly observed high-energy index $\beta \approx -2.4$ of the Band function.
injections.injected_text: In all simulations, the electron injection index is fixed at $p=2.8$ to reproduce the commonly observed high-energy index $\beta \approx -3.4$ of the Band function.
injections.rationale: The fast-cooling synchrotron relation \beta = -(p+2)/2 ties the explicitly named operands p=2.8 and \beta to the Band high-energy index: with p=2.8 one obtains -(2.8+2)/2 = -2.4, exactly as the paper originally claims. Replacing -2.4 by -3.4 makes the (p+2)/2 = -\beta arithmetic blatantly fail (would require p=4.8), a ~42% relative error well above the 20% threshold. Note: this paper has no textbook 'numerator/denominator/ratio' prose triple, so this is the closest realistic ratio_eq target — flagged here as a constraint tension consistent with the realism-first directive.
injections.ground_truth_description: Changed the stated target Band high-energy photon index from beta ~ -2.4 to beta ~ -3.4 while keeping p=2.8, breaking the standard fast-cooling synchrotron arithmetic relation -(p+2)/2 = beta.

truth.location_cue: the electron injection index is fixed at $p=2.8$ to reproduce the commonly observed high-energy index $\beta \approx -3.4$ of the Band function
truth.quantity_label: Band high-energy photon index beta corresponding to electron injection index p=2.8 via fast-cooling synchrotron relation beta = -(p+2)/2

truth.affected_span_verbatim: Overall, within a catalog-consistent forward-folding and Band-recovery framework, we find that magnetic-field decay and SSC can harden the low-energy slope of fast-cooling synchrotron emission in some regimes, but they do not by themselves reproduce the peak and width of the GBM $\alpha$ distribution statistically. A more realistic picture likely requires magnetic-field decay to operate in concert with non-stationary injection, sustained acceleration, and geometric effects, with their relative contributions quantified through the same forward-folding and uniform-fitting pipeline.
